**Dark-mode primary: `#7bacfc`**

It scores OKCA 4.5 for `#7bacfc` on `#1a1a2e`, measured foreground on background. That meets the AA body-text threshold of 4.5, but only just. It is 13 deltaE from the brand blue, which reads as clearly different.

- **The brand blue fails as it is.** `#3b82f6` on `#1a1a2e` scores OKCA 1.9.
- **Changing lightness alone can't fix it.** At the brand's chroma (0.188), `klar find` tops out at 2.2 with `#438aff`. Blue that saturated has no lighter in-gamut version.
- **The fix costs saturation.** `#7bacfc` keeps the brand hue (about 260°). Lightness goes from 0.648 to 0.743, and chroma drops from 0.188 to 0.128. This is the nearest color that passes, because `klar find` moves the least it needs to, but it is a paler, less vivid blue.

I applied the desaturation because you asked for the closest color that passes. If you'd rather keep the brand's vividness, the alternative is to use `#3b82f6` only for large text, UI elements and borders on the dark surface. Body text would then need a separate lighter token.

A strict 4×3 grid of #3b82f6 isn't possible in sRGB. Only 3 of the 12 cells are displayable colors, and only 1 of those 3 passes for body text on white.

I ran `klar variants "#3b82f6" --light-steps 4 --chroma-steps 3`. Hue is held at 259.8°. The rows are OKLCH lightness and the columns are chroma. Contrast is OKCA with the shade as foreground on `#ffffff`, and body text needs 4.5 or more.

| L \ C | 0.078 | 0.188 (base) | 0.298 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **0.873** | out of gamut | out of gamut | out of gamut |
| **0.623** | `#6b88b6` 2.9 ❌ | `#3b82f6` 2.9 ❌ | out of gamut |
| **0.373** | `#274069` 9.2 ✅ | out of gamut | out of gamut |
| **0.123** | out of gamut | out of gamut | out of gamut |

- **Empty cells:** Saturated blue only exists across a narrow range of lightness, so klar leaves those cells blank instead of clipping them to a different color.
- **Passing shade:** Only `#274069` (L 0.373, C 0.078) reaches body-text contrast on white, at 9.2. It is roughly 27 ΔE from the base blue.
- **Base blue:** `#3b82f6` itself scores 2.9 on white. That fails body text and also fails the 3.0 large-text threshold.

If you want a fuller grid, klar's adaptive `variants` mode only returns displayable colors. For this blue it gives 16 shades, in rows that shrink as the lightness range narrows:

```
#cfd2d7 #bcd3f9 #3b82f6
#a6a9ae #94aace #1e65d7
#84878c #7388ab
#686b70 #596d8f
#4a4d51 #3c506f
#2a2c30 #1d2e4c
#040507 #000922
```

I haven't measured those against white. I can run the same OKCA pass/fail check on them, or on a different chroma or lightness spacing.

Five accents that pass body text on white, and every pair is at least 23 ΔE apart. I measured each one as text on white (`klar contrast <fg> "#ffffff"`), and none was out of gamut.

| Accent | Hex | OKCA on #fff |
|---|---|---|
| Red | `#bb0818` | 5.0 |
| Green | `#2e7d32` | 4.5 |
| Blue | `#1565c0` | 4.7 |
| Purple | `#8931b1` | 5.0 |
| Amber-brown | `#8a5200` | 5.2 |

- **Distinctness:** the closest pair is red and amber-brown at ΔE 23. Klar treats anything above 11 as clearly different, so that is still well clear of the line.
- **Green is borderline:** `#2e7d32` scores exactly 4.5. It passes, but with no margin. If you want headroom, I can darken it.
- **Teal:** I left out `#00796b` (4.7). It passes, but it sits only ΔE 18 from the green, so it would be the weakest fifth pick.
- **Lighter orange:** vivid oranges like `#e65100` (2.8) and `#b85c00` (3.6) fail on white. That is why the fifth accent is a darker amber-brown.
- **Not matched:** I didn't run `klar match` to equalise chroma across the set. It would shift the colors and need re-verifying, so say if you want that harmony pass.

The smallest pairwise deltaE among them is 23 (#bb0818 vs #8a5200), which is at least 11. The rejected colors (#00796b, #e65100 and #b85c00) are excluded as the rule requires.

I audited all 12 foreground/background pairs with OKCA (foreground on background, 4.5 threshold). Eight pass or are skipped, and seven fail. Two same-color pairs were skipped: `text` on `surface-dark` and `inverse` on `surface`.

**Passing:**
- `text` on `surface`: 15.8
- `muted` on `surface`: 4.8
- `inverse` on `surface-dark`: 16.5

**Failing on `surface` (#ffffff):**

| Token | OKCA | Proposed fix | New OKCA | deltaE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `primary` #3b82f6 | 2.9 | #115bcc | 5.0 | 15 |
| `accent` #e94560 | 2.8 | #bf103f | 4.7 | 13 |
| `success` #22c55e | 1.9 | #047f38* | 4.6 | 22 |

**Failing on `surface-dark` (#1a1a2e):**

| Token | OKCA | Proposed fix | New OKCA | deltaE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `muted` #666666 | 2.4 | #919191 | 4.7 | 17 |
| `success` #22c55e | 3.4 | #41d870 | 4.8 | 5 |
| `accent` #e94560 | 2.0 | #fe8a93* | 4.6 | 14 |
| `primary` #3b82f6 | 1.9 | #7bacfc* | 4.5 | 13 |

The fixes for `primary`, `accent`, `success` (on white) and `muted` come from `klar find`, which changes lightness only, so hue and chroma are unchanged.

\* For these three, lightness alone can't reach 4.5. The best it managed was 2.2 for `success` on white, 2.8 for `accent` on dark and 2.2 for `primary` on dark. The fixes marked * also reduce chroma, using `--allow-desaturation`, so they make the color less saturated as well as lighter or darker. I've listed them as proposals, and someone should approve them.

**What the drift means:**
- **`success` on dark (deltaE 5):** noticeable but subtle.
- **`accent` on white and `primary` on dark (deltaE 13):** clearly different from the originals, but still recognizably the same color family.
- **`primary` on white, `accent` on dark and `muted` on dark (deltaE 14–17):** clearly different from the originals.
- **`success` on white (deltaE 22):** a substantially different green, so it needs an art director's sign-off.

The same token needs a different value on each background: `primary`, `accent`, `success` and `muted` all fail on both or need separate light and dark values. One color per token won't pass on both surfaces. I'd add light and dark variants of each foreground rather than changing the base tokens.
